facts.title: Automated Tensor Scheduling for Hybrid CPU-GPU LLM Inference on Consumer Devices
facts.event_hint: arXiv paper published 2026-07-11 on tensor-granularity hybrid CPU-GPU inference for consumer device LLM deployment
facts.problem: LLM weights often exceed GPU memory capacity on consumer devices (laptops/desktops), making offloading necessary. Existing offloading systems use coarse layer-level or expert-level scheduling, overlooking intra-layer tensor heterogeneity. They also use load-unaware policies that don't respond to changing device conditions (thermal throttling, background interference). CPU execution becomes the new bottleneck after PCIe transfer optimization.
facts.mechanism: ATSInfer combines three mechanisms: (1) Asynchronous CPU-GPU scheduling to coordinate storage, data movement, and computation across heterogeneous backends, (2) Static tensor placement to determine GPU residency under memory and switching-cost constraints, (3) Load-aware dynamic transfer adjusting runtime tensor movement based on inference phase and backend load. Uses Zero-Copy on RTX GPUs to enable SM-driven transfers overlapping with Copy Engine.

evidence.claim: Improves prefill throughput by up to 1.94x over llama.cpp
evidence.condition: Same GPU VRAM budget, consumer device platforms

evidence.claim: Improves decode throughput by up to 3.29x over llama.cpp
evidence.condition: Same GPU VRAM budget, consumer device platforms

evidence.claim: Increases average GPU utilization during decode by about 70%
evidence.condition: Decode phase, consumer device

evidence.claim: Load-aware rescheduling triggers when deviation exceeds 15% with minimum interval of 5x recent TPOT
evidence.condition: Minimum re-scheduling interval equal to five times recent TPOT, ~9ms overhead

evidence.claim: Evaluated on RTX 3060 (6GB) laptop and RTX 4090 (24GB) desktop platforms
evidence.condition: Laptop: Intel i7-11800H, 32GB DDR4, PCIe Gen4 x16. Desktop: Intel i7-11700, 64GB DDR4, PCIe Gen4 x16

facts.evaluation_context: Implemented by extending llama.cpp with ~15,000 lines of C++ code. Evaluated on two representative consumer platforms: mid-range laptop (RTX 3060 6GB, Intel i7-11800H, 32GB DDR4) and high-performance desktop (RTX 4090 24GB, Intel i7-11700, 64GB DDR4). Models tested: GLM-Z1-9B, Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, GPT-OSS-20B (RTX 3060); Llama3.1-70B, Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, GPT-OSS-120B (RTX 4090). Both dense and MoE models.
facts.limitations: Evaluation limited to two NVIDIA GPU platforms (RTX 3060 laptop, RTX 4090 desktop). Thermal wall on laptop causes TPOT fluctuations. No reported performance/power efficiency metrics. No comparison with server-grade hardware or other consumer GPU vendors (AMD, Intel). Implemented via llama.cpp extension - portability to other inference frameworks unclear.
facts.project_relevance: ATSInfer addresses memory interface and data movement for local LLM deployment on consumer devices. Uses PCIe Gen4 x16 bandwidth with two transfer paths (Copy Engine and Zero-Copy SM-driven). Tensor-granularity placement vs. layer/expert-level is the key innovation for memory-constrained devices. Load-aware scheduling responds to consumer device variability (thermal throttling, background interference). However, the paper does not report HBM/HBF bandwidth (uses GDDR on RTX), performance-per-watt, or peak compute utilization. The focus is on data movement optimization (PCIe transfer reduction via tensor placement) not compute acceleration.

facts.title: REMOP: REmote-Memory-aware OPerator Optimization
facts.event_hint: REMOP framework for remote-memory-aware database operator optimization
facts.problem: Classical disk-spilling operator heuristics minimize I/O volume but can trigger excessive transfer rounds under remote memory where each round incurs fixed RTT, making total latency sensitive to round count
facts.mechanism: Transfer-round-aware intra-operator buffer partitioning strategies; derives operator-specific input/output buffer splits for blocked nested-loop join, external merge sort, and external hash join to minimize total latency L = D/BW + C*RTT

evidence.claim: REMOP reduces transfer rounds by up to 97% and operator runtime by up to 48% on spill-heavy microbenchmarks
evidence.condition: BNLJ single-operator query, selectivity f=1/256K, memory budget M=4K pages, two-node compute-memory testbed

evidence.claim: REMOP reduces BNLJ runtime by 48.7% and transfer rounds by 97.1% at L-optimal buffer settings
evidence.condition: BNLJ with (rin=0.4, pR=0.6), selectivity f=1/256K, M=4K pages

evidence.claim: REMOP lowers average runtime of spilling TPC-H queries by 22.7%
evidence.condition: TPC-H spilling queries, two-node compute-memory testbed

evidence.claim: REMOP lowers average runtime of spilling TPC-DS queries by 26.4%
evidence.condition: TPC-DS spilling queries, two-node compute-memory testbed

evidence.claim: REMOP achieves gains up to 51% under higher remote-memory latency
evidence.condition: Higher RTT sensitivity experiments

facts.evaluation_context: Two-node compute-memory testbed; DuckDB implementation; TCP-based REMON and RDMA-based Infiniswap backends evaluated; microbenchmarks for BNLJ, EMS, EHJ; end-to-end TPC-H and TPC-DS spilling queries
facts.limitations: Testbed evaluation only; no production deployment data; RDMA backend (Infiniswap) shows software overhead and page-granularity mismatch that can diminish raw RDMA advantage; model assumes fixed budget M and does not address dynamic memory redistribution across concurrent queries; RTT parameter tau proportional to BW*RTT must be estimated for deployment
facts.project_relevance: Topic alignment strong (内存语义、DSA卸载: remote memory/disaggregated memory semantics). REMOP addresses memory resource semantics by exposing transfer-round cost structure of remote memory swapping—directly addressing how memory tier changes latency characteristics. Demonstrates端到端收益传导: operator-level microbenchmark gains (48% runtime reduction, 97% transfer-round reduction) propagate to TPC-H (22.7%) and TPC-DS (26.4%) query-level improvements. No DSA/IAA offload focus, but quantifies CPU/data-movement cost of remote memory semantics through RTT-dominated cost model.

facts.title: Formal Foundations for Known Good Reliable Die Screening in Chiplet-Based AI Systems-on-Chip
facts.event_hint: KGRD (Known Good Reliable Die) formal screening methodology for chiplet-based AI SoCs
facts.problem: Conventional Known Good Die (KGD) screening guarantees pre-assembly functional correctness but offers no probabilistic assurance of post-assembly reliability lifetime for expensive chiplet-based AI SoCs
facts.mechanism: Bayesian probabilistic risk model with quantified observability bias bound, safety-gated decision architecture with provable post-assembly failure probability guarantee, Bayes-optimal disposition thresholds, and constrained closed-loop feedback

evidence.claim: Monte Carlo simulation on N=4,000 synthetic dies verifies four theoretical properties
evidence.condition: Monte Carlo simulation on synthetic dies

evidence.claim: Calibration error epsilon-delta = 0.133
evidence.condition: Simulation verification

evidence.claim: Optimal threshold alpha-r* = 0.167
evidence.condition: Bayes-optimal decision theory derivation

evidence.claim: Parameter error reduced by 42% from 1.35 to 0.78
evidence.condition: Constrained MAP update for T=20 iterations with 200 cumulative dies per iteration

evidence.claim: Safety-compliant fraction remains above 98% at every iteration
evidence.condition: Closed-loop feedback verification

facts.evaluation_context: Monte Carlo simulation study on N=4,000 synthetic dies; no real silicon, fabrication process, or production data
facts.limitations: Simulation-only validation; no experimental results on actual ATE/PTE fab data across multiple foundries and packaging technologies; treats package context vector as fixed and fully known; treats dies independently ignoring thermal/mechanical coupling in 2.5D/3D packages; uses logistic model which may miss nonlinear interactions
facts.project_relevance: Topic alignment confirmed (AI芯片与加速器: chiplet/先进封装/KGRD screening). This is a formal/theoretical contribution establishing mathematical foundations for chiplet reliability screening, not an architecture or performance paper. Value is in establishing post-assembly reliability probability guarantees with quantified observability bias bounds—relevant for chiplet-based AI SoC yield and cost modeling. No实测算力、带宽、功耗 data; focus shifts from functional correctness (KGD) to reliability lifetime (KGRD) screening under incomplete pre-assembly observability.

facts.title: An Internet for the KV Cache: Rethinking Classical Infrastructure Boundaries in the LLM Inference Age
facts.event_hint: Vision paper proposing global-scale KV Cache content distribution system
facts.problem: Model-side KV Cache optimizations and system-side transfer/storage optimizations evolve independently within legacy cloud boundaries, preventing optimal placement of compute and KV Cache storage across clouds and datacenters
facts.mechanism: Proposes 'Internet for the KV Cache' vision where KV Cache management works as content-distribution system with global control plane (directory service, placement planner, prefetch scheduler) enabling store-anywhere-use-everything with bandwidth-aware movement and reuse-horizon-based tiering (hot/warm/cold)

evidence.claim: Transferring 1 GB KV Cache over fully utilized 10-Gbps link is ~19x faster and ~5.2x cheaper than AWS 8xB200 GPU cluster compute
evidence.condition: 1 GB KV Cache transfer over fully utilized 10-Gbps link

evidence.claim: Storage-compute locality is core restriction in cloud pricing due to egress costs dominating bulk data movement
evidence.condition: Wide-area cloud movement is slow and egress prices dominate cost

evidence.claim: KV Cache reuse horizons span seconds to hours in agentic workflows, enabling temporal slack for storage-compute tradeoffs
evidence.condition: Agentic workflows with multi-step reasoning, tool calls, code execution

evidence.claim: Placement governed by jointly considering reuse rates, deadlines, bandwidth, transfer and recomputation costs
evidence.condition: Model metrics (prefill FLOPs, KV size), infrastructure metrics (GPU/storage cost, bandwidth), application metrics (reuse frequency, turns)
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 1, Abstract and PDF Page 2, Introduction section

evidence.claim: Paper positions as 'call for arms' rather than implemented system
evidence.condition: Vision paper without concrete implementation or evaluation

facts.evaluation_context: Vision paper without empirical evaluation. Quantitative examples drawn from public cloud pricing documents and prior work. Proposes three-tier storage model (hot near GPU, warm intermediate, cold distant) driven by reuse horizons. References existing systems: SkyPilot, SkyServe for inter-cloud compute; Mooncake for disaggregated KV Cache; various cache compression/eviction techniques. Supplement provides storage-recompute decision formulas comparing model-side (PrefillTFLOPs/KVMB) versus infrastructure/application-side ratios, and decision table across models (DeepSeek V4-Pro, V4-Flash), clouds (AWS, GCP, Azure, GMI), and reuse horizons (1 day, 1 month). Mentions scheduling systems: SOLA (state-aware per-iteration scheduling), ThunderServe (placement and rescheduling across heterogeneous GPUs), SeeSaw (dynamic re-sharding), Libra (SLO-aware batching).
facts.limitations: Vision paper without implemented system or end-to-end evaluation. Transfer cost comparison assumes fully utilized 10-Gbps link; real-world WAN conditions with congestion, variable latency not modeled. No quantitative assessment of control plane overhead, consistency mechanisms, or failure handling. Does not address multi-tenant security or cache poisoning risks. Supplement provides theoretical cost decision framework but no empirical TTFT/TPOT/P95 measurements, no control plane latency overhead analysis, and no consistency/eviction/isolation mechanisms. Decision table shows framework applicability but not production performance data.
facts.project_relevance: Directly addresses TPN project questions on whether network can感知 KV Cache placement and whether network-side optimization adds value beyond GPU memory scheduling. Vision proposes network as active distribution channel where bandwidth/latency/pricing directly determine KV Cache management. Supplement reinforces this with explicit cost decision formulas and scheduling system references. However, lacks concrete TTFT/TPOT measurements or comparison to state-aware network scheduling. No implementation to validate whether proposed global control plane actually improves token throughput or P95 latency versus current cloud-local approaches. Decision table shows storage vs recompute choices but not actual latency improvements.

evidence_gaps.question: What are the quantitative TTFT, TPOT, or P95 latency improvements from implementing the proposed Internet for KV Cache versus current cloud-local approaches?
What are the control plane overheads for KV Cache directory lookup, placement planning, and prefetch scheduling in real-time inference workloads?
How does the proposed system handle consistency, eviction, and multi-tenant isolation across regions and clouds?
